title: Sasaram - The Historic Gateway of Bihar | Complete Travel Guide
content:
Sasaram

Sasaram is one of Bihar’s most culturally significant cities, renowned for its architectural marvels, historical monuments, and natural landscapes. Once the seat of power of the Sur Empire under Sher Shah Suri, Sasaram is dotted with impressive mosques, tombs, lakes, and ancient structures that showcase the state’s glorious past.

Whether you're a history buff, a nature lover, or a traveler looking for offbeat destinations, Sasaram is an unforgettable destination.

History of Sasaram

  • The name Sasaram is believed to be derived from Sahasra Arjuna, a mythological king.
  • Historically ruled by the Shershah Suri dynasty, Mughals, and later the British.
  • The city is home to the world-famous Sher Shah Suri Tomb, an architectural masterpiece built in 1545 AD.
  • Sasaram was also a strategic location during Sher Shah Suri’s rule over northern India.
  • The region finds references in ancient texts and has archaeological significance due to its forts, caves, and inscriptions.

Top Attractions in Sasaram

1. Sher Shah Suri Tomb

The Sher Shah Suri Tomb is Sasaram’s most iconic monument, standing beautifully in the middle of a lake. Its Indo-Afghan architectural style and stunning reflection on the water make it one of the finest historical structures in India.

2. Rohtas Fort

Rohtas Fort, built on the Kaimur Hills, is one of India’s largest forts, offering wide views of the surrounding region. Its ancient gateways, temples, and military structures reflect the fort’s rich historical importance.

3. Tomb of Hasan Khan Suri

The Tomb of Hasan Khan Suri showcases a blend of Afghan and Mughal architecture. Surrounded by greenery, this peaceful site honors the father of Sher Shah Suri and is a calming stop for history lovers.

4. Maa Tara Chandi Temple

Maa Tara Chandi Temple is a sacred Shakti Peeth located inside a natural cave. The temple attracts many devotees, especially during Navratri, and is known for its spiritual energy and unique cave atmosphere.

5. Manjhar Kund & Dhua Kund Waterfalls

These two scenic waterfalls near Sasaram come alive during the monsoon, offering a refreshing escape into nature. They are popular among photographers and travelers seeking natural beauty.

6. Indrapuri Barrage

Indrapuri Barrage across the Son River is a relaxing picnic spot with calm water views. It’s a great place to unwind and enjoy the peaceful surroundings.

7. Gupta Dham (Gupteshwar Mahadev)

Gupta Dham is a cave shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, surrounded by hills and natural beauty. The site is ideal for both devotees and trekking enthusiasts looking for a serene spiritual experience.

Best Time to Visit

  • October to March - Pleasant weather for sightseeing.
  • Avoid peak summer due to high temperatures.

How to Reach Sasaram

By Road

  • Well-connected via NH-19 (Grand Trunk Road).
  • About 150 km from Patna and 120 km from Varanasi.

By Train

  • Sasaram Junction (SSM) is a major railway station on the Howrah–Delhi route.

By Air

  • Nearest airport: Varanasi Airport (120 km)
  • Gaya Airport (130 km) is another option.

Where to Stay

  • Mid-range hotels near Sasaram Junction.
  • Guest houses and lodges near Tara Chandi Temple.
  • For better options, many travelers stay in Dehri-on-Sone.

Travel Tips

  • Visit Sher Shah Suri Tomb in the morning for clear photography.
  • Waterfalls are slippery during monsoon-be cautious.
  • Rohtas Fort requires considerable walking and light trekking.
  • Wear comfortable shoes.
excerpt: Sasaram, located in the Rohtas district of Bihar, is a historically rich town known for its magnificent monuments, including the tomb of Sher Shah Suri. A blend of Mughal architecture, natural beauty, and ancient heritage makes Sasaram a unique travel destination. From waterfalls to forts, the town offers a complete cultural and historical experience.
